rationale: The answer keeps the two measures separate and correct. It defines tracking error as the standard deviation of daily fund-minus-benchmark returns over the agreed one-year window. It defines tracking difference as the cumulative return gap. Adding √252 annualization is a reasonable convention, not an error. Placing fee drag under tracking difference fits the grader note: it never claims a constant daily fee raises the standard deviation of daily active returns. It covers most central causes: sampling/optimization versus full replication and active weights, cash drag/buffers, index reconstitutions/rebalances and corporate actions, pricing and closing-price timing, fair value, stale prices, dividend accrual/withholding, trading costs and timing, and creation/redemption flows. 'Caps' and 'liquidity-constrained holdings' partly cover diversification limits. Minor omissions: variable expenses are not named as a source of variability. It does not explicitly say that a constant fee shifts the mean but not the variance. It does not explicitly say the benchmark and measurement method must be agreed before diagnosis. FX items are largely incidental for a US equity index ETF but not wrong. No material error.
